body.content: Contradiction: The expert's intuition is itself a 'checklist' — an internalized, implicit one. The debate may collapse if we view expertise as implicit psychometric decomposition. If so, the panel's advantage is not 'checklist vs. intuition' but 'explicit aggregation vs. implicit integration.' The question then becomes: does explicit aggregation cancel more noise than implicit integration? If the expert's implicit checklist is well-calibrated (high internal reliability), the panel's explicit aggregation may add no value. This reframes the problem in terms of internal vs. external psychometric structure.
body.why_keep_this: This is a unifying reframe (SRC_003) that dissolves the dichotomy. It is speculative but may inspire a candidate that treats expert intuition as a latent variable model.
